articles.title: Bending Spoons to buy collaboration tools maker Miro for $1.36B, 90% less than its 2022 valuation
articles.description: Bending Spoons is buying Miro for $1.36 billion, a huge dip in valuation for the workplace collaboration startup, which was valued at $17.5 billion in late 2021.
articles.raw_content: Bending Spoons is buying Miro for $1.36 billion, a huge dip in valuation for the workplace collaboration startup, which was valued at $17.5 billion in late 2021.
articles.selection_reason: A $17.5B unicorn selling for $1.36B is the clearest signal yet of the SaaS valuation reset every board must reckon with.
articles.audience_value: A benchmark for repricing late-stage SaaS assets and a lens on the PE-style roll-up playbook Bending Spoons is executing.
articles.why_this_matters: Why this matters: Leaders holding 2021-era valuations need to recalibrate exit expectations and M&A strategy before the market does it for them.

articles.title: OpenAI and Anthropic are making 10 times more revenue than all Chinese AI models combined, research group Rhodium says
articles.description: Rhodium Group's latest analysis of Chinese and U.S. AI companies also found that low revenue did not necessarily correspond with lower valuation.
articles.raw_content: Rhodium Group's latest analysis of Chinese and U.S. AI companies also found that low revenue did not necessarily correspond with lower valuation.
articles.selection_reason: Rhodium's data quantifies the US-China AI revenue gap, reframing the competitive landscape leaders are planning against.
articles.audience_value: Hard numbers on monetization vs. valuation across the two AI superpowers, useful for vendor selection and geopolitical risk planning.
articles.why_this_matters: Why this matters: Executives betting on AI partners need to know where the revenue, not just the hype, is actually accruing.

articles.title: Jensen Huang explains why Nvidia will grow an astounding 70% next year
articles.description: Nvidia has its finger in every pie, and sees another year of plenty in its future, Jensen Huang says. But, he insists, its deals are not circular.
articles.raw_content: Nvidia has its finger in every pie, and sees another year of plenty in its future, Jensen Huang says. But, he insists, its deals are not circular.
articles.selection_reason: Jensen Huang's 70% growth forecast sets the tone for AI infrastructure spending across the entire economy next year.
articles.audience_value: Insight into Nvidia's demand visibility and its rebuttal to circular-deal concerns, informing capex and compute procurement plans.
articles.why_this_matters: Why this matters: If Nvidia is right, compute costs and supply constraints will remain the defining variable in every leader's AI budget.

articles.raw_content:
California Gov. Gavin Newsom (D) is positioning the state to take the lead on AI oversight, including the potential to mandate a "kill switch" for frontier models, with a new executive order issued Friday.

Newsom's order directs the state to convene a group of experts that will deliver recommendations within two months on how to strengthen AI safety measures in state law.
